title: typedef-add-spec
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> typedef add --id <id> <spec.json>`: a reusable type, given as `kind` plus the same per-kind block a field takes in `field-add` (an ENUM declares `enum.values`, a restricted STRING `string.pattern` or a length). It carries only the type: group, name, requiredness, label and metadata keys are rejected with RK_UNKNOWN_ARG, and its descriptions and annotations are set with `meta <id>`. `typedef add --id <id> --kind <K>` covers a bare easy kind; this spec covers the rich ENUM and restricted kinds. Validated against the real kernel before writing. (`--kind` and this spec are mutually exclusive.)

kind.description: STRING | NUMBER | DATE | TIME | DATETIME | DATERANGE | DATEFRAGMENT | BOOLEAN | CONFIRM | ENUM | CUSTOM

minLength.description: minimum character length. seeAlso: the Length operator — the rule-level way to bound length (`operators Length`)

pattern.description: Anchored Java Pattern. A non-empty pattern requires patternMessage, which patternMessages does not replace; an empty one is inactive and needs none. It must be valid Java syntax and avoid A12's blacklist: possessive quantifiers, (?<… / (?>…), \A \G \Z \z \a \e \p \Q \E (lowercase \p only; \P is admitted) and nested unescaped [. The blacklist reads the source text, so an escaped metacharacter before a quantifier (a\*+) is refused too. Passing does not prove JavaScript portability. seeAlso: the PatternViolated/PatternMatched operators, the rule-level alternative (`operators PatternViolated`).

patternMessage.description: The base error text when the pattern fails, applied to every declared locale patternMessages does not override. A non-empty `pattern` without it is rejected: 'a pattern and its error message must be set together'.

patternMessages.description: Per-locale pattern error texts. With a non-empty pattern each entry overrides patternMessage for its locale, and patternMessage remains the required fallback. Entries for undeclared locales are preserved. Without a pattern, entries are still preserved and validated by the kernel, and their legality depends on the declared locales and the text.

noValueValidation.description: Skip the kernel's per-value validation (base64 blobs, attachment content, etc.). Requires lineBreaks:true, else MVK_STRING_TYPE_NO_VAL_AND_NO_LINE_BREAK. A raw-type field's VALUE is then unusable in rules and computations, presence checks only; the one value-shaped exception, a whole-condition Length(f) > c, is a max-length declaration the kernel eliminates (`dmtool diagnostics MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE`). `field read` returns it as string.noValueValidation.

suggestions.description: per-locale hint list, { "<locale>": ["…"] }; validated against the field's own pattern

maxFractionalDigits.description: the decimal scale; together they bound the fraction-digit range

min.description: minimum value (decimal as a string). seeAlso: the LessThan/GreaterThan comparison operators — rule-level bounds

minLength.description: minimum character length of the rendered stored-number text; sign and decimal separator count

maxLength.description: maximum character length of the rendered stored-number text; this is the Date/Time component declaration gate, not maxIntegerDigits

maxIntegerDigits.description: maximum digits before the decimal separator; sign and fractional digits do not count

positivesOnly.description: Forbid a sign (default false: signed). A minus, even on zero, is the formal error zahlMitVorzeichen; a signed field reports a minus zero as zahlNullEnthaeltVorzeichen instead. It also flips the empty-operand FILL polarity: an unsigned empty number can be filled bigger, never smaller. A negative min beside it is valid, and the sign refusal still fires. seeAlso: min — a non-negative min bounds the value without changing the sign polarity.

values.description: ≥1 { value, labels? } — stored value + optional per-locale labels. seeAlso: FieldValueIncludedInValueList / FieldValueNotIncludedInValueList — the rule-level way to (dis)allow a value set

categories.description: named classifications; each has values[] aligned 1:1 with the enum values. seeAlso: the EnumCategory operator (`operators EnumCategory`) — reads a value's category in a rule

description.description: optional editor-level note for the category (the kernel core ignores it; preserved for the editor's Category table)

values.description: values aligned 1:1 with the enum values

sValue.description: The stored-token S-value, the model's INDEX default: when this enum is a repeatable group's index field, full validation transiently supplies it for a nonmandatory index left absent or empty on the parent's only row, while partial validation silently suppresses that cell. Must name a declared value, checked at authoring — the kernel stages it into evaluation unvalidated.

invalidValueMessage.description: error text for an out-of-domain value — one text expanded across ALL declared locales (the shorthand)

errorMessages.description: per-locale invalid-value error text, { "<locale>": "<text>" } — wins over invalidValueMessage; must cover every declared locale (omit both to use the kernel default)

format.description: Case-sensitive Java pattern from one fixed whitelist shared by DATE, TIME and DATETIME, keyed on the string, not the kind. The thirteen: yyyy-MM-dd, dd.MM.yyyy, yyyyMMdd; yyyy, yyyy-MM, yyyyMM, MM, MM-dd, MMdd, ddMM, dd.MM.; HH:mm:ss; yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss. Separators count: MM.yyyy, MM-yyyy, yyyy/MM and dd.MM are refused (dd.MM. with the trailing dot is admitted, and dd.MM is a DATERANGE format only). Case counts (MM months, mm minutes), and no all-lowercase or all-uppercase spelling is admitted, so the editor's UPPERCASE labels (YYYY-MM-DD) are not values: copy a spelling exactly. Default yyyy-MM-dd.

precision.description: FULL (default) | DAY_OPTIONAL | MONTH_OPTIONAL | YEAR_OPTIONAL; every precision still admits fully known dates

rejectBefore1900.description: Deprecated and without effect: A12 stores youngerThan1900Check but does not evaluate it, so a lower bound on dates needs a rule. Accepted so read output round-trips; default false.

format.description: a Java pattern from the shared temporal whitelist (see date.format). HH:mm (no seconds) is rejected, while a date pattern such as yyyy-MM-dd is admitted on a TIME field. Default HH:mm:ss.

Case-sensitive Java date+time pattern, conventionally the ISO instant yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss, though any of the thirteen temporal patterns (see date.format) is admitted; check the exact form with `field add --dry-run`.

Case-sensitive Java date pattern for both endpoints, from a fixed set independent of locale and conditionLanguage. The (format, separator) PAIR is allowlisted, never the format alone: see `separator` for the twelve admitted pairs. Formats: dd.MM.yyyy, yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy, yyyy-MM, MM, MM-dd and dd.MM; yyyyMM is a legal DATE format but not a DATERANGE one, and dd.MM the reverse. Case counts (MM months, mm minutes), and no all-lowercase or all-uppercase spelling is admitted, so the editor's UPPERCASE labels (YYYY-MM-DD, MM/MM, …) are not values: copy a spelling exactly.

separator.description: The separator PAIRED with `format`; exactly twelve pairs are admitted: - with dd.MM.yyyy or dd.MM, and / or the empty separator (read as /) with yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy, yyyy-MM, MM or MM-dd. Everything else is refused as 'The date range format is invalid': every separator swap, a '.' separator with any format, a spaced ' - ', and yyyyMM with any separator.

interpretationOfYear.description: Matters only for a yearless range that wraps the year end (01.11-31.01 on dd.MM, otherwise start-after-end and invalid): the endpoint that keeps the base year while the other moves, the reverse of what the names suggest. FROM rolls the end forward a year, TO rolls the start back. The default, STANDARD (both endpoints in the base year), has no spelling: omit the key, since the tokens STANDARD, PREVIOUS and SUBSEQUENT are refused. Effective only when the model declares a base year (`config modify`).

rejectBefore1900.description: Deprecated and without effect: A12 stores youngerThan1900Check but does not evaluate it, so a lower bound on dates needs a rule. Accepted so read output round-trips; default false.
Deprecated and without effect: A12 stores youngerThan1900Check but does not evaluate it, so a lower bound on dates needs a rule. Accepted so read output round-trips; default false.

format.description: Case-sensitive Java pattern, conventionally a partial date (MM, yyyy, yyyy-MM, MM-dd), though it admits the same thirteen patterns as DATE/TIME/DATETIME (see date.format). Case counts (MM months, mm minutes), and no all-lowercase or all-uppercase spelling is admitted, so the editor's UPPERCASE labels (YYYY, YYYY-MM) are not values: copy a spelling exactly.
